pr_title: feat: Convert request id to string of base 36 and prefix it with `req-`
pr_body:
Prefix the request id with a `req-` string and convert the auto incremented request id (of type number) to string using the base of 36.

✅ Closes: #2736

issue_context.title: Have default request id generation generate unique id:s
issue_context.body:
## 🚀 Feature Proposal

Currently request id:s default to an auto-incremented number, but that number is generated locally in each instance, meaning that if one run two or more instances of Fastify, or restarts a single Fastify instance, then the default generated id:s will be duplicated between between two or more requests:

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/453028bbfbb34a240bddb146549d91261deac495/lib/reqIdGenFactory.js#L3-L9

Instead truly unique string id:s should be generated, by eg. using @mcollina's performant [hyperid](https://github.com/mcollina/hyperid) module.

## Motivation

The general expectation of a request id is that it should uniquely identify a request, across instances and across time. The current solution solves neither.

(Minor bonus motivation: Also, the common style of request id:s is that they are quite long unique text strings, whereas Fastify currently is a bit odd in that it generates an actual number rather than a string, possibly giving people a false impression, as Fastify do persist any incoming `x-request-id` header and few of those will likely be a number. If a developer has assumed that a request id is actually always a number, then that could cause some issues as well.)

## Example

If I want to track down all logs that belong to a single request and filter all of those logs using the request id, then the expectation should be that any log point with the request id of that single request is caused by that request – either within the same application logs or in services called by the current instance and where the request id has been forwarded.

Currently, with a restarted fastify instance or an horizontally scaled fastify instance, the logs of multiple different requests all share the same request id, making the request id in such cases much less useful.

## PR

I can help make a PR if there's agreement on this.
comments: Is this a proposal to make this  https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Server/#genreqid the new default?

Yes, make the suggestion there the new default:

> Especially in distributed systems, you may want to override the default id generation behaviour as shown below. For generating UUIDs you may want to checkout hyperid

Regarding distributed systems we usually use the `Trace-Id` like mentionned here: https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/#trace-id and those IDs are generated with another process (like nginx for example); offloading fastify.

> Currently, with a restarted fastify instance or an horizontally scaled fastify instance, the logs of multiple different requests all share the same request id, making the request id in such cases much less useful.

One thing would be to identify the instance itself to add request-id in correlation with the instance ID. I faced this issue and i added an uuid to the instance.

> One thing would be to identify the instance itself to add request-id in correlation with the instance ID.

I think this is pretty much what hyperid does. It generates a unique id for the instance and an auto-incremented id to those, thus getting the speed of auto-increments with the uniqueness of UUIDs. (I think it refreshes the unique ID every once in a while as well, to eg not run out of ID:s in long running instances)

On tracing id:s: I would say they are meant for tracing services in particular, like AWS XRay, Jaeger, OpenTelemetry, and can identify a sub-trace within the larger request trace, whereas request id:s are more general purpose and always identifies the original request and is mostly used for eg logging.

> > One thing would be to identify the instance itself to add request-id in correlation with the instance ID.

> I think this is pretty much what hyperid does. It generates a unique id for the instance and an auto-incremented id to those, thus getting the speed of auto-increments with the uniqueness of UUIDs. (I think it refreshes the unique ID every once in a while as well, to eg not run out of ID:s in long running instances)

The point is having possibility to identify the instance itself and not the request in what i'm saying, to use the ID of the instance on other purposes. Which for example in a log viewer would lead to a query like:
```
request-id = "42" && instance-id = "foo-bar-123"
```

The “instance” part is easy: you can add name to the logger instance.

> request-id = "42" && instance-id = "foo-bar-123"
> ```

I feel that any identifying of instances is out of scope of the request id in general  and this issue in particular.

One can never assume that the request id will be generated by this piece of code and it will only ever be able to identify the instance that generated the id and I don’t see how that’s very useful?

Maybe open a new issue dedicated to any such wish?

Not sure if I'm missing something, but I think the current implementation is fine.
If you want to have unique request ids you should override the default implementation.
The reason why currently it is a incremental integer, is that if you don't need that feature, it will cost you close to nothing the fact that we are running it :)

We could improve the documentation section to highlight this. What do you think?

> Not sure if I'm missing something, but I think the current implementation is fine.
> If you want to have unique request ids you should override the default implementation.

What's the point of a request id that isn't unique?

> The reason why currently it is a incremental integer, is that if you don't need that feature, it will cost you close to nothing the fact that we are running it :)

If I don't have use for a unique request id, when would I ever have use for a non-unique request id?

I would say: Either remove the current default all together and default to have no request id:s, or implement proper request id:s. Sounds like of those two choices you would prefer removing the feature @delvedor?

I'm with @delvedor. The feature should remain as it is. Request id generation and propagation is far more complicated that just slapping a UUID on new requests. Providing the feature as it is, offers those who need to customize it can and aids developers locally with an easy to follow id.

I suspect that most people who care about this feature will already be using some sort of OpenTracing/OpenTelemetry setup anyway. So the request id Fastify generates will be of very little use.
Also one other downside would be a bit harder to read logs by default, which are already quite verbose, I think it is best to keep it very straightforward by default.

> If I don't have use for a unique request id, when would I ever have use for a non-unique request id?

This feature is "good enough", in the sense that non-unique request ids could be easily made unique from context when a _human_ is reading the logs. Note that we have `hostname` and `pid` to disambiguate. I've _never_ had a use for unique ids in non-tracing scenarios (and then those are governed by the span/trace mechanism).

My 2 cents on this: In a microservice/distributed world it is very important to have unique reqids and to propagate them thru the services in order to have a proper inspection of the req/res cycle. I really like that fastify supports it. On the other side, I am not sure that making this the default would benefit newcomers. If someone needs to have unique reqids across multiple replicas of the service he/she is already skilled enough to properly implement it.

Ok, so no hyperid request id generation in core then, but how about making the default at least be something that looks and feels like the string it is rather than is an auto-incremented integer?

Just changing from `1` to `'req-1'` would help clarify the nature of it + if you want to keep it less verbose, then the number could be formatted in hexadecimal or base64 representation to ensure it stays short even after many many requests have been made.

> Ok, so no hyperid request id generation in core then, but how about making the default at least be something that looks and feels like the string it is rather than is an auto-incremented integer?

I think that is a fair compromise.

I might be a month late, but is this already implemented?
If not and if it is up for grabs, may I have a chance to provide a MR for this issue?

> Just changing from `1` to `'req-1'` would help clarify the nature of it + if you want to keep it less verbose, then the number could be formatted in hexadecimal or base64 representation to ensure it stays short even after many many requests have been made.

I agree that using base64 representation of the request _id_ (number) as `req-<base64_number_representation>` would make it less verbose.
I would actually recommend to use `.toString(36)` instead. It's less compact than `base64`, but it would significantly faster to generate. Anyway, it's up for grabs.

review_comments: This output would be `req-1` if i'm not wrong. Was it wanted?

I asked because I read the issue and I understood that the outcome would be a string like the "base64", so it was not clear to me

In this case I'm not sure what should do the to String(32) function since the variable is a number

After joining a discussion on the issue it was concluded that a prefix of `req-` should be added alongside of converting the number to a string with a base of 36.

`toString` method on the `Number.prototype` returns a string representing the specified number (on which the method was called) using the specified `radix` (base).
This will return a string representing the number from the `10` base (in the example you provided `1`) to a string with a base of `36` (which in the same example will result in the value `1`, like in the base 10).

However, the difference comes for the numbers greater than 9.
i.e. for the number value `25752` (base 10) the output would be `64a2` (base 36).

To better understand this please do refer to the following (taken from [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Errors/Bad_radix)):

> The optional radix parameter of the Number.prototype.toString() or the BigInt.prototype.toString() method was specified. Its value must be an integer (a number) between 2 and 36, specifying the base of the number system to be used for representing numeric values.

> The most common radixes:
2 for binary numbers,
8 for octal numbers,
10 for decimal numbers,
16 for hexadecimal numbers.

I apologize if I completely misunderstood your question and just stated the obvious, but just wanted to give a little background of the change and why was the `toString(36)` used in this context.

Also, these comments were the ones on which the implementation was based upon:
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/2736#issuecomment-745247740
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/2736#issuecomment-777382265
Thanks for the explanation, I was not aware of the `toString` supports the `base` parameter too!
